title: Conjecture 4
statement_text: For every integer $k\geq 3$, there exists a set $X$ of vertices and a set $C$ of $k$-colorings of $X$ such that no $X$-rooted-$K_{k}$-minor-free graph $G$ realizes $C$.
context_text: A set of $k$-colorings of a set $X$ of vertices is a set $C$ of functions $f:X\to[k]$ closed under permutations of the colours ($f\in C$ implies $\pi\circ f\in C$ for every permutation $\pi$ of $[k]$). A graph $G$ realizes $C$ if $X\subseteq V(G)$ and a function $f:X\to[k]$ belongs to $C$ if and only if $f$ extends to a proper $k$-coloring of $G$. For $X\subseteq V(G)$, an $X$-rooted minor of $G$ is a minor whose model can be chosen so that every branch set contains a vertex of $X$; $G$ is $X$-rooted-$H$-minor-free if $H$ is not an $X$-rooted minor of $G$. DeVos and Seymour proved that every set of $3$-colorings of a cyclically ordered set $X$ is realized by a plane graph with $X$ on the outer face in that order, hence by an $X$-rooted-$K_4$-minor-free $K_5$-minor-free graph; this limits the method of reducible configurations for $3$-coloring. The authors generalise this: for every $k\ge3$, every set $C$ of $k$-colorings of any $X$ is realized by some $X$-rooted-$K_{k+1}$-minor-free $K_{k+2}$-minor-free graph, so reducible configurations cannot exploit global properties when fewer colours are used than Hadwiger's conjecture postulates. The conjecture says this does not extend to $X$-rooted-$K_k$-minor-free graphs. It is a weakening of Holroyd's strengthening of Hadwiger's conjecture: if $G$ is $k$-colorable and every $k$-coloring of $G$ uses all $k$ colours on $X$, then $K_k$ is an $X$-rooted minor of $G$; Holroyd proved this for $k=3$ and Martinsson and Steiner for $k=4$.
paper_title: A note on extendable sets of colorings and rooted minors
